item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers presented the fifth annual Tommy Lasorda I Bleed Dodger Blue Award to Charlie Hough and Joe Amalfitano on Sunday.
The honor is bestowed every season to members of the Dodgers community who embodies the passion, enthusiasm and love for the team that former Hall of Fame manager Tommy Lasorda possessed.
Hough and Amalfitano were recognized during an on-field ceremony before the series finale against the San Francisco Giants. Laura Lasorda, Tommy’s daughter, presented the awards with the ceremony taking place two days before what would have been her father’s 99th birthday.
Charlie Hough
Hough has now spent 46 years in the Dodgers organization as a player, coach or special assistant in the baseball operations department. The Dodgers drafted Hough in the eighth round of the 1966 MLB Draft.
Hough went on to make his MLB debut with the team in 1970, and pitched for the Dodgers in 11 of his astounding 25 seasons. While with L.A., the right-hander went 47-46 with a 3.50 ERA and 60 saves over 401 games (16 starts).
Hough retired after making 21 starts for the then-Florida Marlins in 1994. He was 46 years old at the time.
Overall in his career, Hough finished with a 216-216 record and a 3.75 ERA in 858 games (440 starts).
Joe Amalfitano
Amalfitano, 92, served 14 seasons as third base coach on Lasorda’s Dodgers staff from 1983-96. He also was a senior adviser in baseball operations from 2002-04. Overall, Amalfitano amassed 67 seasons in professional baseball as a Major League player with the New York/San Francisco Giants, Houston Colt .45s and Chicago Cubs (1954-67).
Amalfitano’s baseball career also included serving as manager with the Cubs (1979-81) and a front office executive. As a player, Amalfitano collected 418 hits across 10 seasons in the Majors.
Tommy Lasorda Bleed Dodger Blue Award history
The inaugural Tommy Lasorda Award went to Rosalind Wyman, who was the key figure in bringing the Dodgers to Los Angeles from Brooklyn in 1958.
She additionally was influential in helping the Giants relocate from New York while also helping the Lakers move to Los Angeles from Minneapolis.
The second annual Tommy Lasorda Bleed Dodger Blue Award went to John Shoemaker in 2023, and Steve Yeager was the recipient in 2024.
For 2025, the Dodgers presented the Tommy Lasorda I Bleed Dodger Blue Award to longtime public relations executive Steve Brener and Hall of Fame broadcaster Jaime Jarrín (2025). Coincidentally, Hough joined Laura for the on-field ceremony to celebrate Brener and Jarrín.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Kyle Tucker didn’t start on Sunday, one day after fouling a ball off his right knee, but the Dodgers right fielder insisted that he felt fine. This was more of a chance to pair a rest day for Tucker with Monday’s scheduled off day for the team.
“[The off day] wasn’t planned. I just felt that after he took one off the knee, this would have been 10 in a row for him,” manager Dave Roberts said Sunday. “He’s playing well, played a lot. It’s a chance to give him two days, then six in a row to finish the season.”
The injury was in a much higher spot on his leg than the right shin fracture that cost him two months on the injured list during the 2024 season while with the Houston Astros.
Tucker did pinch-hit in the eighth inning on Sunday, and he’s second on the Dodgers in games played (148), starts (141), and plate appearances (602), trailing only Freddie Freeman in all three categories. Tucker is playing the best baseball of his season at the moment with five home runs in his last 10 starts, hitting .417/.500/.972 since September 9.
Notes
Speaking of playing in the outfield on Tuesday, the Dodgers will likely activate center fielder Andy Pages off the injured list to play in the series opener against the San Diego Padres, after he missed the last 27 games after a fastball broke his left hand on August 21.
Pages at the end of this season will have two years, 155 days of major league service time and will be eligible for salary arbitration for the first time as a Super Two player, among the top 70 percent in service time among major leaguers with two years but not yet three years of service time. MLB Trade Rumors last week projected the cutoff for Super Two players this offseason to be two years, 134 days.
Longtime Dodgers third base coach Joey Amalfitano and knuckleballer Charlie Hough were honored on the field at Dodger Stadium prior to Sunday’s game as the 2026 winners of the the Tommy Lasorda I Bleed Dodger Blue Award. This is the fifth year of the award, timed close to Lasorda’s birthday, which is Tuesday.

Joe Amalfitano and Charlie Hough Win Tommy Lasorda I Bleed Dodger Blue Award
LOS ANGELES – The Los Angeles Dodgers today named Charlie Hough and Joe Amalfitano as recipients of the Tommy Lasorda I Bleed Dodger Blue Award, an honor bestowed every year since 2022 to members of the Los Angeles Dodger community who embody the passion, enthusiasm and love for the Dodgers that the Hall of Fame manager possessed. The award will be presented today by Lasorda’s daughter Laura before the Dodgers’ 1:10 p.m. game against the San Francisco Giants, two days before what would have been Lasorda's 99th birthday.
Hough, 78, has spent 46 years in the Dodger organization as a player, coach and special assistant in the Baseball Operations department, dating back to his selection by the franchise in the eighth round of the June 1966 Amateur Draft. Making his MLB debut for Los Angeles in 1970, Hough pitched 799.2 innings in 401 games for Los Angeles with a 3.50 ERA, including 60 saves and a franchise record 204 relief appearances of at least two innings. Retiring from the Majors at age 46 in 1994 with the Marlins, he finished with a 216-216 career record and 2,362 strikeouts across 3,801.1 innings and 858 games, with a 3.75 ERA.
Amalfitano, 92, served 14 seasons as third-base coach on Lasorda’s staff from 1983-96, as well as Dodger senior adviser in baseball operations from 2002-04. Overall, Amalfitano amassed 67 seasons in professional baseball as a Major League player with the New York/San Francisco Giants, Houston Colt .45s and Chicago Cubs (1954-67), manager with the Cubs (1979-81) and front office executive. As a player, Amalfitano collected 418 hits across 10 seasons in the Majors.
The previous winners of the Lasorda award include longtime public relations executive Steve Brener (2025), Hall of Fame broadcaster Jaime Jarrín (2025), former catcher Steve Yeager (2024), longtime Minor League manager John Shoemaker (2023) and former Los Angeles City Councilmember Rosalind Wyman (2022).
The Los Angeles Dodgers franchise, with nine World Series championships and 26 National League pennants since its beginnings in Brooklyn in 1890, is committed to a tradition of pride and excellence. The Dodgers, baseball’s 2024 and 2025 back-to-back World Champions, are the reigning Sports Business Journal Sports Team of the Year, have been recognized as ESPN’s Sports Humanitarian Team of the Year and are dedicated to supporting a culture of winning baseball, providing a first-class, fan-friendly experience, and building a strong partnership with the community. With the highest cumulative fan attendance in Major League Baseball history and a record of breaking barriers, the Dodgers are one of the most cherished sports franchises in the world. item.content:encoded:
Robert De Niro is in talks to play Tommy Lasorda - the Hall of Fame manager who became one of the most recognizable figures in Los Angeles Dodgers history - in a new sports film.
The two-time Oscar winner, 83, is being courted for the project, which carries the working title Tommy & Me and is being developed at Skydance Sports.
The film would mark another entry in De Niro's long list of larger-than-life real and fictional characters.
Tommy Lasorda's Legacy
Lasorda spent 71 years with the Dodgers, the longest association any person has had with the team. He began as a player in the Brooklyn era before moving through the ranks as a scout and coach. He went on to manage the club for two decades, winning two World Series titles and earning their induction into the Baseball Hall of Fame.
His connection to the team never ended. In his later years, Lasorda took on an advisory and ambassador role, scouting, mentoring and turning up at Dodger Stadium in a seat near the dugout he once ran.
He died in 2021 at 93, remembered as much for his fiery personality and devotion to the Dodgers as for his on-field success.
Casting Is Still Being Finalized
De Niro is still in negotiations for the lead role, and plot details are being kept under wraps, with no word yet on how the film will approach Lasorda's life and career, according to Deadline.
The creative team is further along. Reid Carolin, who directed the 2022 Channing Tatum film Dog and wrote Magic Mike's Last Dance, is set to direct from a script he wrote with George Gallo and Cambron Clark.
Skydance Sports' Growing Catalogue
The project fits a growing pattern for the studio. Skydance Sports has moved from documentaries into narrative films built on real sports stories, a shift that includes the Ben Affleck-directed Air and the upcoming Mr. Irrelevant.
Lasorda is a natural subject for that treatment, as he remains one of the most celebrated and quotable managers the sport has produced, while his decades in the Dodgers dugout gave the franchise some of its defining moments.
De Niro's Lengthy Career
De Niro won Academy Awards for The Godfather Part II and Raging Bull, in which he famously played boxer Jake LaMotta, and remains one of the most acclaimed actors of his generation through films including Taxi Driver and Goodfellas.
He's stayed busy well into his 80s, most recently starring in the Netflix thriller The Whisper Man.

item.content:encoded:
Two-time Academy Award winner Robert De Niro will portray another legendary sports figure in an upcoming film, according to a published report.
De Niro, 83, who won an Oscar for portraying middleweight boxing champion Jake LaMotta in the 1980 film “Raging Bull,” is in talks to play Los Angeles Dodgers Hall of Fame manager Tommy Lasorda, Deadline reported.
The film, tentatively called “Tommy and Me,” will be produced by Skydance Sports with Reid Carolin as director, according to the entertainment sports website.
No details have been released about the angle the film will take in depicting the garrulous manager, who “bled Dodger blue” as Los Angeles’ colorful manager from 1976 to 1996.
Lasorda, who compiled a 1,599-2439-3 record with the Dodgers, won four National League pennants and two World Series in Los Angeles. He was inducted into the National Baseball Hall of Fame in 1997 by the Veterans Committee.
Lasorda, who died on Jan. 7, 2021, at the age of 93, spent only three seasons in the majors as a left-handed pitcher and had an 0-4 mark. He broke in with the Philadelphia Phillies organization in 1945, but spent the majority of his career as a member of the Dodgers.
He played 11 seasons in the minors for the franchise when it was based in Brooklyn and Los Angeles, and spent 10 season managing Dodger minor leaguers until joining the major league team in 1973 as a third-base coach.
He replaced longtime manager Walter Alston in 1976 and then carved out his own niche as the Dodgers’ skipper, being named N.L. Manager of the Year in 1983 and 1988. He was also the N.L. manager in four All-Star Games.
In addition to “Raging Bull,” De Niro won a Best Supporting Actor Oscar for “The Godfather Part II” as a young Vito Corleone. He has received nine Oscar nominations overall, with other lead actor roles in “Taxi Driver” (1976), “The Deer Hunter” (1978) and “Awakenings” (1990).
De Niro was also nominated for Best Supporting Actor in “Cape Fear” (1991), “Silver Linings Playbook” (2012) and “Killers of the Flower Moon” (2023). He was also nominated for Best Director for the 2019 film “The Irishman.”
The actor also had memorable roles in “Goodfellas” and “Casino.”

Según señala Deadline, citando fuentes cercanas a la producción, el título provisional de la película es Tommy & Me. Entre sus próximos proyectos, Carolin dirigirá Isle of Man, un drama deportivo sobre carreras de motos.
En cuanto a De Niro, el reconocido actor ganador de dos premios Oscar, tiene pendiente el estreno de Ahora los suegros son ellos el próximo 27 de septiembre. Tommy & Me sería su segundo biopic tras su interpretación en Toro salvaje, película que le valió la estatuilla a mejor actor principal en 1981.
Lasorda mantuvo durante 71 años una relación con los Dodgers, siendo la más duradera en la historia del equipo
Nacido en Pensilvania y descendiente de inmigrantes italianos, Lasorda inició su trayectoria en el béisbol profesional al firmar con los Philadelphia Phillies en 1945. En 1949, debutó en las ligas menores con los Brooklyn Dodgers, aunque solo jugó como titular en un encuentro. Su carrera como jugador se caracterizó por las dificultades, pero su verdadero legado comenzó a construirse tras retirarse como jugador.
En 1960, tras la creación de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, se unió al equipo como ojeador. En 1973, el entonces entrenador, Walter Alston, lo incorporó como entrenador de tercera base con miras a que eventualmente lo sucediera. Finalmente, cuatro años después, cuando Alston se retiró, Lasorda tomó las riendas del equipo.
Durante dos décadas al frente de los Dodgers, Lasorda logró cuatro títulos de la Liga Nacional y dos campeonatos de la Serie Mundial. En sus últimos años, continuó como asesor del equipo, involucrándose en la formación de nuevos talentos y asistiendo a entrenamientos. Además, era habitual verle en el Dodger Stadium como espectador, siempre cerca del banquillo que ocupó como entrenador.

item.content:encoded:
Robert De Niro en la película Fanático - TRISTAR PICTURES


   MADRID, 16 Sep. (CulturaOcio) -
   Robert De Niro se encuentra en negociaciones para dar vida a Tommy Lasorda, el entrenador de los Dodgers fallecido en 2021, en un biopic sobre su vida que prepara Skydance Sports. Lasorda, una de las figuras más destacadas de la historia reciente del béisbol, estuvo más de 70 años vinculado a los Dodgers, primero como jugador y, posteriormente, como entrenador.
   Según informa Deadline citando fuentes cercanas a la producción, su título provisional es Tommy & Me. Reid Carolin (Magic Mike, Dog. Un viaje salvaje) será el encargado de dirigir la cinta, cuyo guion firman George Gallo, Cambron Clark y el propio Carolin. Por el momento, se desconocen detalles sobre el enfoque que adoptará el filme para narrar la historia de Lasorda.
   Carolin también produce la película a través de Free Association, sello del que es socio junto a Channing Tatum. Entre sus próximos proyectos, el cineasta tiene previsto dirigir Isle of Man, drama deportivo centrado en las carreras de motos.
   En cuanto a De Niro, que acaba de estrenar en Netflix el thriller Susurran tu nombre, el dos veces ganador del Oscar tiene pendiente el estreno de Ahora los suegros son ellos, la nueva entrega de la saga de comedia que protagoniza junto a Ben Stiller, el próximo 27 de septiembre. Tommy & Me sería el segundo biopic de su carrera tras Toro salvaje, que le valió la estatuilla a mejor actor principal en 1981.
Además, De Niro ya se adentró en el mundo del béisbol en Fanático, el filme de Tony Scott en el que daba vida a un inquietante aficionado obsesionado con los San Francisco Giants y con su nuevo fichaje, el antaño mejor jugador al que dio vida Wesley Snipes. La película se estreno en 1996 y se presentó en el Festival de cine de San Sebastián.
TOMMY LASORDA, LA LEYENDA DE LOS DODGERS
   Nacido en Pensilvania e hijo de inmigrantes italianos, Lasorda dio sus primeros pasos en el béisbol profesional cuando fichó por los Philadelphia Phillies como agente libre amateur en 1945. Cuatro años más tarde, debutó en las ligas menores con los Brooklyn Dodgers, aunque solo jugó como titular en un partido.
   Su carrera como jugador estuvo llena de dificultades, y su legado verdadero legado comenzó comenzó a forjarse una vez colgó los guantes. En 1960, los recién creados Dodgers de Los Ángeles lo contrataron como ojeador, y en 1973, el entrenador del equipo, Walter Alston, lo fichó como entrenador de tercera base, con vistas a que acabara convirtiéndose en su sucesor. Efectivamente, cuatro años más tarde, una vez que Alston se jubiló, Lasorda asumió el cargo al frente del equipo.
   Durante sus veinte años como entrenador, Lasorda conquistó cuatro títulos de la Liga Nacional y dos campeonatos de la Serie Mundial. En los últimos años de su vida, ejerció como asesor del equipo, colaborando en la búsqueda de talentos y en los entrenamientos. También era habitual verlo en el Dodger Stadium, en un asiento situado cerca del banquillo que ocupó como entrenador.
   En total, Lasorda estuvo vinculado a los Dodgers durante 71 años de su vida, la relación más longeva que alguien ha mantenido con el equipo.

item.content:encoded:
An all-time Los Angeles Dodger great is the subject of a new Hollywood production.
Tommy Lasorda, the longtime Dodgers manager, will be the titular character of the new biopic “Tommy & Me,” report Matt Grobar and Justin Kroll of Deadline.
Lasorda, who pitched briefly for the Dodgers back in Brooklyn, is perhaps best remembered as the team’s manager from 1976 to 1996.
In that time, he won four National League pennants and a pair of World Series titles, eventually earning a spot in the National Baseball Hall of Fame.
“His reputation as one of baseball’s most beloved and recognizable figures only grew with age. A passionate ambassador for both the Dodgers and the city of Los Angeles, he died in 2021 at 93,” Grobar and Kroll wrote.
So who else could portray this Dodgers legend besides a legend of the silver screen?
Who will play Tommy Lasorda in the new movie?
Tommy Lasagna will be played by another Italian-American legend: Robert De Niro.
The “Godfather Part II” and “Goodfellas” actor is in talks to play Lasorda, Deadline reports.
And he’s not the only established Hollywood name involved in the production.
The Skydance Sports production is to be directed by Reid Carolin, best known for his work with producing partner Channing Tatum, and the script is being written by Carolin, George Gallo and Cambron Clark.
What will the movie be about?
Given De Niro’s age of 83, it seems likely that he’ll play an older adult Lasorda.
The 1988 World Series, the Dodgers’ final championship before this recent spate of three titles in six years, would certainly make an interesting setting.
Orel Hershiser in his prime, Kirk Gibson’s World Series homer, it all seems readymade for the big screen.
That said, De Niro has done some de-aging work, like in “The Irishman,” so perhaps the film will include earlier moments from Lasorda’s life as well and use AI to make De Niro appear younger.
In any case, it’s the kind of project that’s surely to get baseball fans excited and lead to theaters packed full of Dodgers fans in Southern California.
There’s no telling how long this movie will take to come to fruition, but do you plan on catching it once it comes out?

item.content:encoded:
The legacy of Tommy Lasorda is expected to hit theaters in the near future, and it’s believed to have one of Hollywood’s finest playing the Hall of Fame Los Angeles Dodgers manager.
Robert De Niro is in talks to play Lasorda in the upcoming film “Tommy & Me,” according to Deadline,
Details have yet to emerge as to what approach the film will take in telling Lasorda’s story, but the script will be led by George Gallo, Cambron Clark and Reid Carolin. Skydance Sports is expected to help produce the movie that will highlight one of baseball’s most iconic figures.
Lasorda, known for his fiery spirit and larger-than-life personality, is one of the most iconic managers in Dodgers history, as he helped coach and manage the team from 1973 through 1996, leading them to two World Series titles in 1981 and 1988, and being crowned National League Manager of the Year in 1983 and 1988.
In 1997, the Dodgers retired his No. 2 jersey, the same year he was immortalized in the National Baseball Hall of Fame.
After his managing career came to an end, Lasorda became an impactful member of the Dodgers front office, serving as a vice president, senior vice president, and special advisor from 1998 to 2021, where he is credited with making a large impact, such as helping scout and sign Mike Piazza.
In 2021, the Dodgers announced that Lasorda had passed away at a hospital near his home in Fullerton.
Before working as a coach and in front offices, Lasorda’s start in baseball began in 1954 as a player with the Dodgers, when they were still located in Brooklyn.
His playing career didn’t last too long, as he spent his first two seasons with the Dodgers and was later sold to the Kansas City Athletics in 1956.
Lasorda spent the next four years in the Minor Leagues and would retire from playing following the 1960 season.
De Niro, who is known for being able to play characters that have a fiery passion like Lasorda, has been in many notable films during his acting career, including Taxi Driver, The Godfather Part II, and Goodfellas.

item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE: With Paramount Pictures Mr. Irrelevant already gaining buzz prior to its holiday opening, Skydance Sports is looking to hit a home run with its next big pic on one of the more iconic baseball figures in the past 50 years. Sources tell Deadline that Oscar winner Robert De Niro is in talks to play Tommy Lasorda, the legendary Dodgers manager, in a new sports pic going by the working title Tommy & Me with Reid Carolin directing for Skydance Sports.
There are no details yet as to the approach the film will take in chronicling Lasorda’s story.
The script is by George Gallo, Cambron Clark and Carolin. Skydance Sports is serving as lead studio, with Jesse Sisgold, Jason T. Reed, Sandino Moya-Smith producing for the company, alongside Mandalay Pictures’ Peter Gube, Intuition Productions’ Keri Selig and Diane Galardi, and Reid and Garret Livetz for Free Association.
Watch on Deadline
An iconic ambassador for the Dodgers organization, Lasorda began his career as a player for the Philadelphia Phillies, embarking on a brief stint in the U.S. Army and going back to the minor leagues before making his way to the Brooklyn Dodgers in 1949. He spent most of his brief playing career in the minors, though he pitched for a time for both the Dodgers and the Kansas City Athletics.
Lasorda’s greater impact on his sport came behind the scenes in the Dodgers organization, where he elevated over time from scout to minor-league manager to the major-league coaching staff. He joined as third-base coach in 1973 — under Hall of Fame manager Walter Alston — became the Dodgers’ manager in 1976 and led the club until 1996. During his time as manager, he guided Los Angeles to four National League pennants and World Series championships in 1981 and 1988.
Lasorda was named National League Manager of the Year in 1983 and 1988, managed four All-Star Games, was named to the National Baseball Hall of Fame in 1997 and saw his No. 2 jersey retired by the Dodgers. After retiring from the Dodgers dugout, he managed the U.S. baseball team at the 2000 Sydney Olympics, leading the squad to defeat the heavily favored Cuba and win gold.
